::: {.alert .alert-warning}
**The app is the supported way to run RiboPilot.** The functions on this page do
the same work from R, for scripts. They skip some of the app's checks, and you
still need the app for the Taxonomy step and for export groups. Do not run them
while the app is running a workflow for the same project.
:::

# Run the pipeline

```r
status <- RiboPilot::run_assembly("~/my_project")
```

This does the same work as **Update** then **Run from App**: it runs every
sample whose taxonomy is locked and whose State is Ready to run, and returns
Nextflow's exit status (0 means it finished). Like the app, it holds the
project's run lock while it runs, so it stops with a message if another run is
already going for the project.

There is no separate rescue function. To rescue a failed sample, give it an
option set that uses the baited assembler in the app, as in the rescue section
of the [Assemble walkthrough](Test-Project-Assemble.html#rescue-a-sample-that-failed),
then run the pipeline again.

# Build a reference database

This runs on your own computer, not in the container, so it needs Entrez Direct
and the other download tools installed there (the unsupported route; see
[Installing tools without a container](Without-Containers.html)). The Reference
step in the app does the same inside the container.

`RiboPilot::build_reference_db()` takes a standard NCBI search (the same kind
of query you would type on the [NCBI website](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/))
and a short label for the group. First check how many records match; nothing is
downloaded:

```r
RiboPilot::build_reference_db('"Littorinimorpha"[Organism]', "littorinimorpha",
  count_only = TRUE, conda_env = "ribopilot")
```

Then build the database and point a new project at it:

```r
db <- RiboPilot::build_reference_db('"Littorinimorpha"[Organism]', "littorinimorpha",
  out_dir = "~/ribopilot_refs", conda_env = "ribopilot")
RiboPilot::new_project(
  path             = "~/my_project",
  mapping_fn       = "~/my_samples.csv",
  data_path        = "~/my_reads",
  custom_seeds_db  = db$seeds,
  custom_labels_db = db$labels
)
```

`db$seeds` and `db$labels` are the paths of the two files it writes,
`~/ribopilot_refs/seeds/littorinimorpha_rrna_seeds.fasta` and
`~/ribopilot_refs/labels/littorinimorpha_rrna_labels.fasta`.

- **Build once, reuse forever.** If you run `build_reference_db()` again for the
  same group and folder, it reuses what you already built and returns the same
  paths instead of downloading again; add `overwrite = TRUE` to force a fresh
  build.
- **Groups with few sequences.** If your search returns only a handful of
  records, broaden it to a larger group. For example, search a whole family or
  order rather than a single genus, so RiboPilot has enough reference sequence
  to work with.

# Export

`RiboPilot::export_project()` writes one bundle for each export group you made
in the app's Export step, using the "default" header template, and a `.zip` of
each. With no groups, it writes every exportable unit into one bundle named
`export`.

```r
RiboPilot::export_project("~/my_project")
```

`RiboPilot::export_bundle()` writes one group, and can use a header template you
saved in the app:

```r
RiboPilot::export_bundle("~/my_project", group = "fish_batch1", export_opts = "my_template")
```

Both follow the same rule as the Export step: a unit is exported when its sample
is locked in the Assemble step, the unit is locked in the Annotation Review
step, its contig is kept, and it is not excluded from export. Unlike the
app, neither function asks about flagged records; they are exported, with their
flags in the summary CSV.

# Add samples or metadata

`RiboPilot::add_samples()` adds new samples to a project, and
`RiboPilot::update_sample_metadata()` changes the extra columns of samples
already in it. See [Your own project](Your-Own-Project.html).

# Cluster helpers

`RiboPilot::generate_config()` saves a profile for your cluster's scheduler, to
pass to `new_project()` as `executor`. `RiboPilot::hydra_setup()` prepares an R
session on the NMNH Hydra cluster for console runs. See
[Running on a cluster](Clusters.html).
